purpose: Dated exogenous chronology for Afghanistan-specific international intervention and withdrawal. This file declares historical phase boundaries and mission roles only; it does not tune model capacity magnitudes to violence outcomes.

phases.coalition_mission: ISAF expansion plus separate US-led OEF combat mission
phases.notes: NATO-led ISAF expanded north and west while the separate US-led coalition continued operations elsewhere.
ISAF assumed the southern region on 31 July 2006 and the eastern region on 5 October 2006, completing nationwide expansion.

phases.coalition_mission: ISAF combat and security-force assistance during transition
phases.notes: The Inteqal transition to Afghan security lead began in 2011.
Afghan forces took the lead for security nationwide on 18 June 2013; transition completed and ISAF ended in December 2014.

phases.coalition_mission: Resolute Support train, advise and assist
phases.notes: Resolute Support began 1 January 2015 as a NATO-led non-combat mission. Separate US counterterrorism activity is not represented by this phase label and must be sourced separately before implementation.

phases.coalition_mission: Resolute Support train, advise and assist
phases.notes: RSM troop-contributing countries confirmed an increase from about 13,000 to about 16,000 troops in November 2017.

phases.coalition_mission: Resolute Support under withdrawal agreement horizon
phases.notes: The United States and Taliban signed the Doha agreement on 29 February 2020, including withdrawal of international forces.
NATO Allies began the final RSM withdrawal on 1 May 2021; the benchmark ends on 15 August 2021.

sources.title: Agreement for Bringing Peace to Afghanistan

implementation_rule: Do not map qualitative mission phases to model force/capacity values until independent quantitative or categorical evidence supports that mapping.
